beats.text: Your donated books are supposed to end up on somebody's shelf. One box had a thirty dollar tracker hidden inside, and it did not go to a shelf.

beats.text: Here's the stupidly simple version. An AirTag is a coin that shouts its own location. Reporters slipped one into a shipment of donated rare books and followed it. It reportedly ended inside an Amazon facility that trains AI. Books in, model out.
beats.show_cue: Screen recording of the original investigation page, scrolling from its headline down to any tracker map or route screenshots it published.

donated books resold to AI training data

beats.text: So why books? Models learn from text, and books are unusually good text. Long, edited, written by people paid to make sense. One follow-up says Amazon is trashing them for training. One tracked box proves a route, not a policy, and Amazon hasn't answered. Watch this one, don't shout about it yet.
